title: Plant systems
subject: science
strengths: Most of the class can name the roots, stem and leaves and say what each part does.
The class can trace water on its journey from the roots up the stem to the leaves.

modelAnswers.question: What two jobs do the roots do for the plant?
modelAnswers.answer: The roots hold the plant in place in the soil, and they drink up water for the whole plant.

modelAnswers.question: A drop of water is taken in by the roots. What happens to that drop next?
modelAnswers.answer: It travels up the stem to the leaves, where the leaves use it with sunlight to make food.

commonErrors.misconception: Plants take food from the soil through their roots, like we eat food.
commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that the roots are the mouth of the plant and eat food from the soil.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: say what the roots really take from the soil, and which part makes the food.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: the roots drink water and minerals only; the leaves make the food with sunlight.

commonErrors.misconception: Plants take food from the soil through their roots, like we eat food.
commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner says plants eat through their roots because there is food in the soil.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: say why the drinking roots show the plant does not eat like we do.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: plants do not eat at all - the roots drink water and minerals, and the leaves make the food with sunlight.

nextSteps: Reteach the trap, landing that the roots are not a mouth: they drink water and minerals, and the leaves make the food with sunlight.
Practise tracing one drop of water from the roots up the stem to the leaves before answering journey questions.
